tasks.title: Stop the -O child tests from inheriting the operator's real credentials and .env
tasks.why: A plain pytest run is one refactor of main()'s first two lines away from a paid model turn and a live ClickHouse Cloud query against the operator's own cluster.
tasks.notes: From security finding sec2 of improve-merge-cycle-cleanup. READ IT FIRST. Neither -O test requests the `redirected` fixture, so the child gets the developer's full environment and a live core.ROOT, and one of them calls smoke.main(['--target','eks']). CORRECTION TO THE FINDING'S REMEDIATION, verified this cycle: its second half suggests pointing the child at a redirected root 'by inserting a tmp_path on its sys.path instead of the live core.ROOT'. That CANNOT work -- core.ROOT is derived from __file__ (launcher/core.py:12), so the child recomputes the live checkout no matter what sys.path holds, and the child must keep the real root on sys.path to import scripts.smoke at all. Override core.ROOT inside the child's own program text instead, the way the `redirected` fixture does in-process at tests/conftest.py:303-304. require_assertions() is main()'s second line (scripts/smoke.py:537, after parse_args), so it still fires before any .env read -- the root override is defense in depth for the case where that ordering regresses, not a replacement for it.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

optimised() hands the child an environment with every conftest.REDIRECT_KEYS entry removed -- the 21-key union that holds API_KEY, the five CLICKHOUSE_*/OTLP keys and the six LANGFUSE_* keys -- while keeping whatever the interpreter needs to start (PATH, HOME, and PYTHONPATH if set). Passed via core.run(..., env=...), which forwards **kwargs to subprocess.run.

The child cannot read the operator's real root .env: its program overrides core.ROOT (and core.RUNTIME) to a throwaway directory before importing anything that calls config.load_env(). Implemented in the child's program text, not via sys.path -- see the task notes.

Both existing -O tests still assert what they asserted before, including the control assert that proves the child really was optimised (tests/test_smoke_queries.py:280,286). The scrub must not make either test vacuous: if the refusal under test can no longer be reached because the environment is empty rather than because the guard fired, the test has stopped testing the guard.
The scrubbed key set is derived from conftest.REDIRECT_KEYS by reference, not re-listed in this file, so a key added to the union is covered here without a second edit.

A COMMITTED regression test sets a sentinel API_KEY in the parent environment, invokes optimised() with a child program that reports os.environ, core.ROOT and core.RUNTIME, and asserts the sentinel is absent, core.ROOT is not the repository root, and core.RUNTIME is under the redirected root. The test must fail if either the env scrub or the root/runtime override is removed.

issues: ac2: non-blocking - the scrub is a deny-list over REDIRECT_KEYS, so a credential outside the union (e.g. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, OPENAI_API_KEY exported in the operator's shell) still reaches the child. That is exactly what ac5 asks for, so it is the contract rather than a defect, but the residual surface is worth knowing.
verdicts.notes: Full verification command run in the worktree and green (489 passed, +1 vs main; ruff clean; frontend check ok with one pre-existing warning). All five critical ACs verified actively rather than by inspection: the 21-key REDIRECT_KEYS union was read out of conftest by AST and matched to the scrub, the in-child ROOT/RUNTIME override was checked against the fact that load_env() reads core.ROOT only at call time, the two pre-existing -O tests were run individually and their assertions diffed line-for-line against main (unchanged, and each still keyed to a guard-specific message so neither is vacuous), and the new ac6 regression test was subjected to an out-of-tree mutation probe that confirms it fails when either the env scrub or the root override is removed. tasks.title: Make the STATIC_MANIFESTS contract true, or stop claiming it
tasks.why: config.STATIC_MANIFESTS is documented as every manifest applied unchanged and eks check iterates it, but the deploy path applies the two individually -- so a third entry would be parsed by the check and never applied to the cluster.
tasks.notes: NOT a debt item -- this is a latent bug the prior cycle's quality reviewer surfaced OUTSIDE its findings, so it carries no finding id. VERIFIED THIS CYCLE: launcher/eks/config.py:84-86 documents STATIC_MANIFESTS as 'Every manifest under k8s_dir() that is applied unchanged'; launcher/eks/check.py:129 iterates the tuple; but the deploy path applies each one individually in two different functions -- restrict_agent_ingress at launcher/eks/lifecycle.py:154 and deploy_collector at :167. DO NOT collapse the two applies into a loop: they are deliberately ordered and separately post-processed (the policy goes in before the release exists, the collector is applied then waited on then tailed), and lifecycle.py is task 5's file this wave -- see constraint 6. The fix is a guard that the tuple and the applied set cannot silently disagree, plus honest wording. tests/test_eks_deploy.py already records the deploy's process sequence via fake_sh and the Recorder/Steps shape, which is where the applied set can be read.
